result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.is_k_regular()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Check if the graph is k-regular (all nodes have degree `k`). ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L4710-L4795){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.is_k_regular(k) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} A graph is k-regular if every node has degree exactly `k`. For directed graphs, this means all nodes have in-degree `k` and out-degree `k`. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [k]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The degree value to check for. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `True` if the graph is k-regular, `False` otherwise. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} - empty graphs are considered 0-regular - cycles are 2-regular - complete graphs `K_n` are *(n-1)*-regular - path graphs are *not* regular (end nodes have degree `1`, middle nodes have degree `2`) - for directed graphs, checks both in-degree and out-degree equal `k` ## Examples {.doc-examples} Check if a cycle is 2-regular: ::: {#b42bf2a5 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph() graph.add_cycle_graph(6) # Returns True (cycles are 2-regular) graph.is_k_regular(2) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` True ``` ::: ::: ::: {#5bfacd82 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} # Returns False graph.is_k_regular(3) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` False ``` ::: ::: Check complete graph regularity: ::: {#95adb250 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph() n = 5 for i in range(n): graph.add_node(label=f"n{i}") nodes = sorted(graph.get_node_ids()) for i in range(n): for j in range(i + 1, n): graph.add_edge(nodes[i], nodes[j]) # Complete graph K_n is (n-1)-regular; returns True graph.is_k_regular(n - 1) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` True ``` ::: ::: ::: {#ff728f26 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} # Returns False graph.is_k_regular(n) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` False ``` ::: ::: Check isolated nodes: ::: {#6d343423 .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph() graph.add_node(label="A") graph.add_node(label="B") graph.add_node(label="C") # All isolated nodes have degree 0; returns True graph.is_k_regular(0) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ``` True ``` ::: ::: ::: {#8708648d .cell execution_count=6} ``` {.python .cell-code} # Returns False graph.is_k_regular(1) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=6} ``` False ``` ::: :::
